text:
incident-bot: PAGER: oncall_eng - High-severity: streaming runtime memory collapse (decode path) detected in eu-west-1 cluster. Multiple GPU OOMs, container restarts. Auto-pager sent.

ryan_oncall: seeing the alert, joining. Can someone drop the noisy logs?

anne: I pulled the alert stream — decoder processes on pool streaming-eu-2 are spiking mem + OOMs. Recent deploy? Not that I can see.

sara: logs show repeated token-growth loops from a handful of clients: headers show client-max_tokens=10000 while our route default is 512.

mike: confirmed. Sample log:
```
E 1687654319 decode.cpp:421 - CUDA OOM on device 0, requested 14.2GB, free 0.5GB
W 1687654319 request: id=req-9b3a, model=redwood/v2-stream-1, max_tokens=10000, stream=true
I 1687654320 kv_cache: growth detected, entries=1.2M
```

ryan_oncall: that mismatch is the smoking gun. Some clients bypassed route caps (legacy header handling). We should quick-enforce a server-side hard cap.

anne: agree. Enabling decode-throttle feature-flag for streaming tier now. This will clamp max_tokens to 1024 at ingress.

ops-bot: Feature flag "ingress.hard_max_tokens=1024" toggled by anne at 2023-06-24T14:05:12Z :gear: 

sara: also adding a temporary routing rule to steer traffic away from streaming-eu-2 to streaming-eu-1 and streaming-eu-3. Doing a gradual drain (no kill) to avoid request loss.

mike: starting a k8s restart on the two most OOM-prone pods (stream-decode-7, stream-decode-9) after drain completes.

ryan_oncall: what's the customer impact right now? any SLA violations?

support-jen: support queue flagged ~120 dropped streaming requests in the last 12 mins across 3 customers. One enterprise customer (acme-inc) reported timeouts. I'll open support tickets and coordinate a customer note.

anne: drain completed. Routing change pushed. New requests are landing on eu-1/3 and respect ingress.hard_max_tokens. Early telemetry: drop rate down from 3.7% to 0.4%.

mike: restarted pods and bumped node-level KV cache eviction to be more aggressive:
```
eviction.window=60s
kv_cache.max_entries=200k
```
Pods restarted cleanly, no further immediate OOMs.

ops-bot: node stream-decode-7 restarted (pod id 6a7f2). stream-decode-9 restarted (pod id 5c1d0).

ryan_oncall: good. Any signs of persistent runaway generation sources?

sara: correlating request ids — ~90% of the heavy sessions come from a single client token (token prefix xYz). Looks like a buggy SDK version that forgot to cap max_tokens. We should rate-limit that API key and contact the customer.

support-jen: created tickets: SUP-5123 (acme-inc), SUP-5124 (beta-corp). I flagged priority and included suggested mitigation steps for customers (upgrade SDK, add client-side cap).

anne: I'll push a short-term mitigation: reject requests with header-client-max_tokens > 2048 with a 400 + helpful error. Patch going to canary now.

mike: rolling patch to routing layer canaryed at 14:12:30Z. Response sample: 400 {"error":"max_tokens exceeds allowed limit (2048); upgrade client or request lower value)"}

ryan_oncall: telemetry looks stable for 5m. CPU on fallback hosts increased but within thresholds. Need to track post-incident for possible capacity commit.

sara: quick postmortem notes: root cause = client-side misconfig (max_tokens header) combined with missing server-side hard cap at ingress + kv_cache growth not being backpressure-aware. Protection gaps: header parsing legacy path, no global ingress clamp, eviction defaults too permissive.

support-jen: customer comms draft (shared):
"We observed degraded streaming availability for a subset of requests due to runaway generation from client-side requests that requested an excessive number of tokens. We have implemented server-side safeguards and routing mitigations; affected customers have been contacted directly. If you use an SDK, please upgrade to the latest version which enforces sensible token limits."

ryan_oncall: assigning follow-ups:
- anne: permanent ingress clamp + add telemetry alert when header max_tokens > route max (P1)
- sara: make kv_cache eviction reactive to decode memory pressure (P1)
- mike: capacity review for eu cluster and autoscale knobs (P2)
- support-jen: finalize and send customer notices; track impact (P1)

anne: created infra issue INF-2331 for ingress clamp + unit tests.

sara: created infra issue INF-2332 for reactive eviction + perf test.

mike: created ops ticket OPS-117 for capacity sizing, marked P2.

support-jen: customer notes sent for acme-inc and beta-corp, both acknowledged; acme asked for RCA timeframe.

ryan_oncall: leaving this thread open for 2 hours for follow-ups. If no regressions, we'll demote to postmortem doc. Great coordination, team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT: 1687654321 STATUS -> mitigated; severity lowered to reduced-impact at 2023-06-24T14:25:50Z.

ryan_oncall: tagging postmortem doc follow-up in #postmortems and adding timeline.

anne: quick note — saved core dumps and stack traces to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1687654321/ for the research team.

mike: leaving a runbook update: add step to clamp client-provided max_tokens at the ingress layer and document expected per-route maxima.

support-jen: will keep customer tickets open until RCA published.

ryan_oncall: thanks all. I'll hand to oncall rotation. I'll follow up in the postmortem with metrics and graphs.
